items.title: It’s Boom Time in Kyrgyzstan, Courtesy in Part of the War in Ukraine
items.summary: The economy of the Central Asian nation grew by 11 percent last year, partly by becoming a key conduit for goods flowing into Russia.

items.title: Yemen’s Houthis Show Growing Sophistication and Self-Reliance in Weaponry
items.summary: The Houthis are increasingly using artificial intelligence and other tools to produce advanced weaponry on their own, making them less reliant on Iran.

items.title: Alex Saab, Venezuelan Tied to Maduro, Pleads Guilty in Florida
items.summary: Alex Saab, a former official in Venezuela and longtime ally of its deposed leader, Nicolás Maduro, agreed to cooperate with investigators.

items.title: Ukraine and Russia Say There Is No Energy Truce, Despite Trump’s Claims
items.summary: The Kremlin said that an agreement would be “a very good idea” but that any deal would not have much effect on fuel markets, as President Trump had suggested.

items.title: Carney Pitches Canada as a Haven of Investment Stability in a Chaotic World
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney brought together in Toronto about 100 money managers overseeing much of the world’s wealth to promote Canada as an ideal place to invest.

items.title: Gulf Arabs Seek Options After U.S. Bases Did Not Deter Iran
items.summary: The American presence in these countries has not shielded them from retaliation during the Iran war. Now they are hoping direct talks with Iran could help.

items.title: Houthis Report Deadly Saudi Airstrikes as Kingdom Issues Mass Alerts
items.summary: The two sides traded accusations of attacks as fighting inside Yemen remains fierce. The escalating conflict threatens to further destabilize the Middle East.

items.title: Rising Fuel Prices Set Off Anger and Protests Around the World
items.summary: From Indonesia to Guatemala to Syria, shortages and price increases are leading to protests and blackouts.

items.title: An Heir to a Thai Beer Empire Accused His Brother of Sexual Abuse. Then He Took on His Family.
items.summary: Siranudh Scott, an heir to Thailand’s Singha beer empire, has prompted a rare public reckoning about a topic considered taboo.

items.title: Denmark Says Russian Warship Fired Flares at Military Helicopter
items.summary: The incident was the latest in string of episodes involving airspace incursions and other provocations that European leaders have blamed on Russia.

items.title: Age Limits for Social Media Outlined by European Union
items.summary: A proposed law would bar children under 13 from using social media across the 27-nation bloc.

items.title: OpenAI Considers New Financing at a $1.5 Trillion Valuation
items.summary: The funding round would double the value of the start-up behind ChatGPT and establish it as the world’s most valuable private company.

items.title: ‘60 Minutes’ Season Premiere Sees Dip in Ratings
items.summary: Just under 8 million people watched Sunday’s season premiere, down 21 percent from last year. Viewership for the N.F.L. lead-in fell by about the same.

items.title: Steve Bannon and Bernie Sanders Condemn Tech ‘Oligarchs’ and Demand A.I. Reforms
items.summary: At an event in Washington, partisanship took a back seat as elected officials, religious leaders, parents and artists called for reining in artificial intelligence.

items.title: Data Center’s Spill of 5,000 Gallons of Diesel Forces N.J. River Cleanup
items.summary: The fuel poured from a storage tank at a large data center in Secaucus, N.J., into a tributary of the Hackensack River.

items.title: Senate Votes to Block Crypto Bill in Major Blow to the Industry
items.summary: The landmark legislation, known as the Clarity Act, stalled in the Senate as Democrats raised concerns about President Trump’s personal investments in crypto.

items.title: Poverty Rate Was Stable Before Trump’s Safety Net Cuts Gained Force
items.summary: Median household income rose to a record $87,460 in 2025, according to annual Census Bureau data on the financial well-being of Americans.

items.title: The New Restaurant at the Public Theater Revives the Astor Family Name

items.title: Two Chinese Firms Used Binance to Launder Iranian Oil Money, US Says
items.summary: Federal prosecutors said proceeds from the sale of Iranian oil flowed through Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, to finance terrorism.

items.title: With Emmys Haul, Apple Joins the Big Leagues of TV
items.summary: The tech giant took home the most trophies this year, breaking the chokehold HBO and Netflix have had on the awards for more than two decades.

items.summary: On social media, Meta’s chief executive appeared to jab at Anthropic by saying that leading A.I. labs should be focused on safety rather than improving their own technology.

items.title: Is There Anything Google’s Fruit Fly Brain Can’t Do?
items.summary: Models of the insect’s nervous system have been trained to solve a Rubik’s Cube, play video games and even parallel park a car.

items.title: Gates Foundation Pledges $1 Billion to Combat A.I. Inequality
items.summary: Bill Gates, the foundation’s chairman, has been vocal about the dangers of artificial intelligence. The donation will be invested in A.I. projects to bridge social inequalities.

items.title: Alex Bores Wants Democrats to Make AI Safety a 2028 Election Issue
items.summary: Alex Bores, who lost a congressional primary contest that revolved around A.I. regulation, is trying to position himself at the center of the conversation for the next presidential election.
